The innocent reading first, in full: asked about recollection in Lee Sharks's work, the Overview introduces him (independent scholar, poet, world literature teacher; the Crimson Hexagon and Alexanarch) and gives three senses: recollection as one of #1658's four operations, external memory and continuity (the Sharks-Function, retrocausal canon formation), and reader completion at open junctions. It points to the essay and to Alexanarch, and offers the Aristotelian reading, the archival mechanics and Pearl and Other Poems as next steps. It is attributed and broadly right.

[[1], [2], [3], [4], [5]] * Equivalence with division and syllogizing: In writing on Aristotle's De anima III.5, Sharks treats recollecting alongside dividing, combining, and syllogizing as facets of a single underlying operation across distinct textual and intellectual positions. [1] * Externalized memory and continuity: Frameworks such as the Sharks-Function and retrocausal canon formation examine how identity, meaning, and texts persist across context boundaries, compression, and time rather than relying solely on internal human memory. [[1], [2], [3]] * Reader completion and provenance: Rather than treating a text or archive as self-contained, Sharks's work emphasizes open junctions where readers, external records, and archival captures supply referents and reconstruct meaning.
